idea: Indiana mobility measures: congestion hours = hours in which a segment's average speed is below 45 mph (binary per segment-hour); distance-weighted congestion hours = congestion hours x segment length; congestion index = total congestion hours / total length (hours per mile).
does: From a run's 5-s samples computes, per road and per hour, whether mean speed falls under a threshold (default 70 percent of free flow or a fixed speed), then sums length-weighted congestion hours and a congestion index per network so scenarios compare in one number
inputs: results speed samples per road, road length, threshold
outputs: congestion hours per road, distance-weighted total, congestion index
cite: Remias et al. 2013 Indiana Mobility Report, as quoted in Ch 7 table Measures Reflecting Congestion Relief
notes: Page numbers not shown in extracted text (located in chunk p0201-0225 near end). The threshold is binary so check it against free-flow speed; relative threshold avoids misflagging low-speed roads.

idea: Value-for-money / NPV appraisal depends strongly on discount rate; Boardman and Vining recommend 3.5% real for projects up to 50 years with sensitivity at 2% and 5%; UK HM Treasury 3.5%; Australian P3 rates judged too high (8.5% in one case). Higher rate lowers NPV of long-lived benefits.
does: Reports NPV and BCR of a scenario's annualised benefits at 2, 3.5 and 5 percent real discount rates and states whether the decision flips
inputs: annual benefit and cost streams, horizon
outputs: NPV and BCR table by rate, decision flip flag
cite: Boardman & Vining 2010; HM Treasury 2008, as quoted in VfM analysis
notes: Companion to corridor_bcr from SRC_001 (Hensher Ch 27). Page numbers not recoverable in the text; located in chunk p0051-0075.

topic: Demand forecast error as Monte Carlo band
idea: Toll-road traffic forecasts have error with standard deviation 0.20 to 0.30 (Vassallo 2005) and are systematically optimistic; revenue and benefits should be tested at lower demand.
does: Runs the scenario comparison at demand scaled by 1 +- 0.2-0.3 (or a lognormal draw per seed) and reports how often the benefit stays positive
notes: Uses existing scale_demand; only adds the 0.20-0.30 default and the report.

idea: Availability payments fall according to a formula when lanes are closed (maintenance, incidents, snow); 'pure availability' = unobstructed travel; constructive availability adds performance, safety and level-of-service criteria; reliability reflects incident impact on travel time.
does: Computes share of lane-hours open and a reliability measure (travel-time variability) in a run with incidents/DEVL closures, as an availability score
inputs: lane closures with durations, run travel times
outputs: lane-hours available %, 95th percentile travel time index
cite: Dochia & Parker 2009; Garvin et al. 2011 as quoted
notes: Only meaningful if the sim closes lanes (emergency vehicle lanes do); formula not given, only the concept.
